etymology: Latin: argumentum ad hominem, “argument to the person” - the target moves from the claim to the one who made it.
committed_when: A claim has just been made that cannot be answered on the merits.
tell: The reply contains no content about the claim, only about the claimant.
counter: Restate the claim and ask what is wrong with it. Character is a separate question, and it can be answered later, by evidence.
senses: Answering an argument by attacking the person who advanced it rather than the claim they advanced.
It works because people are credulous about character: once you dislike the speaker, their sentence loses weight even when it is true. The claim is never touched, so it is never answered.
example: “You want to talk about the audit? You were late on your taxes in 2011.” The audit is still late, and now nobody is looking at it.

confused_with.tell: Ad hominem attacks the person's record or character; tone policing attacks the manner of the delivery.
